title: UniEdit-Flow: Unleashing Inversion and Editing in the Era of Flow Models
claim: Existing methods fail on reconstruction and edit fidelity in hard cases; ours gives exact reconstruction and edits that preserve unedited regions.
layout: 3 columns by 2 rows, left-to-right: task, baseline, ours. Top row is inversion, bottom row is editing. Emoji/✗ labels sit under the column titles.
description: This is a 3×2 grid of photographs with handwritten-style headings. The left column is titled 'Diverse Existing Tasks' and shows the task inputs. The top-left images are a baseball player in a crowd and a flower-shop storefront, labelled 'Full Prompt / Null Prompt Inversion'. The bottom-left images are a dog, a goat with a cat, and a kitten by a fishbowl, labelled 'Text-driven Image Editing' with edit hints (BG→Water, Goat→Horse, Fish→Frog). The middle column, 'Vanilla Flow', shows failures. The top row has garbled, distorted reconstructions under a sad emoji and 'Large Reconstruction Errors'. The bottom row has edits that drift from the original image, marked with a red ✗ and 'Deviation from the Original Image'. The right column, 'UniEdit-Flow' (bold), shows near-perfect reconstructions under a smiley face and 'Exact Inversion and Reconstruction'. Its edited images keep the background and subjects, marked with a purple heart and 'Satisfactory Customized Editing'. The eye goes first to the garbled storefront image in the middle column.
caption: UniEdit-Flow for image inversion and editing. Our approach proposes a \textit{\textbf{\color{ourpurple} highly accurate and efficient}}, \textit{\textbf{\color{ourpurple} model-agnostic}}, \textit{\textbf{\color{ourpurple} training and tuning-free}} sampling strategy for flow models to tackle image inversion and editing problems. Cluttered scenes are difficult for inversion and reconstruction, leading to failure results on various methods. Our \inversion{} achieves exact reconstruction even in such complex situations (1st line). Furthermore, existing flow editing always maintain undesirable affects, out region-aware sampling-based \editing{} showcases excellent performance for both editing and background preservation (2nd line).
abstract: Flow matching models have emerged as a strong alternative to diffusion models, but existing inversion and editing methods designed for diffusion are often ineffective or inapplicable to them. The straight-line, non-crossing trajectories of flow models pose challenges for diffusion-based approaches but also open avenues for novel solutions. In this paper, we introduce a predictor-corrector-based framework for inversion and editing in flow models. First, we propose Uni-Inv, an effective inversion method designed for accurate reconstruction. Building on this, we extend the concept of delayed injection to flow models and introduce Uni-Edit, a region-aware, robust image editing approach. Our methodology is tuning-free, model-agnostic, efficient, and effective, enabling diverse edits while ensuring strong preservation of edit-irrelevant regions. Extensive experiments across various generative models demonstrate the superiority and generalizability of Uni-Inv and Uni-Edit, even under low-cost settings. Project page: https://uniedit-flow.github.io/
